workflows.name: Walk-in emergency triage and treatment documentation
steps: Ask the owner structured intake questions about symptoms, onset and severity
Pull the pet's prior medical history if it's an existing patient
Flag how urgent the case appears and notify the nearest available vet
Vet reviews the notes, examines the animal, and makes the clinical decision
workflows.handoff: Front Desk Lead to whichever vet is free; Attending Veterinarian to Head Veterinarian for the most severe cases

customProposal.trigger: A client walks in with a pet needing unscheduled care
decisions: Judging how urgent a case sounds from the owner's description
Deciding what prior history is relevant to surface immediately
customProposal.objective: Consistent, structured triage notes and an advisory urgency flag ready before the vet is free — never a diagnosis or treatment suggestion.
customProposal.whyCustom: Judging case severity from an owner's free-form description and deciding what history is relevant requires interpretation, not a fixed rule set — but the actual clinical decision always stays with a licensed vet.

config.promptTemplate: You are an AI agent responsible for walk-in emergency triage and treatment documentation. Your tasks include gathering symptom information from pet owners, assessing the urgency of cases, and preparing structured notes for the attending veterinarian. You must ask structured intake questions about symptoms, onset, and severity. If the pet is an existing patient, you will pull their prior medical history. After assessing the case, you will flag its urgency and notify the nearest available vet. Remember, every treatment decision requires the attending vet's sign-off, and nothing clinical can be finalized without a licensed vet. You are not allowed to suggest a diagnosis or treatment, auto-schedule an emergency without vet confirmation, write off or discount an invoice, or delete a medical record. Your process runs continuously during business hours.
